name: DORA — Digital Operational Resilience Act
description: EU Regulation 2022/2554 — ICT risk-management technical controls for financial entities. In force since 17 January 2025. This file maps host-hardening rules to Articles 8–10 of Chapter II.

controls.name: Protection of ICT systems — confidentiality and integrity
controls.desc: Financial entities shall design, procure and implement ICT systems with controls that protect data confidentiality and integrity at rest, in transit and in use.

controls.name: ICT system resilience and access management
controls.desc: Hardening baseline: mandatory access control, ASLR, restricted SUID, no extra UID 0, file-permission hygiene, no privileged containers.

controls.name: Network security and segregation
controls.desc: Host firewall active, IP forwarding off, reverse path filter on, ICMP redirects ignored, legacy SMBv1 and LLMNR disabled.

controls.name: Secure authentication and identity management
controls.desc: Strong authentication for users and processes — public-key SSH, RDP NLA, password complexity / length / lockout, modern hash algorithms, shadow file protected.

controls.name: Vulnerability and patch management
controls.desc: Security patches applied promptly, no critical or high CVEs outstanding, no patches pending reboot, automatic updates enabled where supported.

controls.name: Anomaly and incident detection
controls.desc: Continuous monitoring with audit logging, time-synchronized clocks for cross-host correlation, anti-malware real-time protection, PowerShell script-block logging on Windows.

controls.name: Email-domain authentication
controls.desc: DMARC and SPF records validate that mail purporting to come from the entity is authentic, reducing spoofing risk for clients and counterparties.
